metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.candidate_universe: Selection rule fixed before collection: examine (1) the official Swift Forums at swift.org/community as the canonical official discussion channel (language-neutral criterion: every assigned language's official/primary community hub is checked identically), (2) Stack Overflow 'swift' tag and historical Stack Overflow Trends/Developer Survey data as the largest general-purpose public Q&A source, (3) Apple Developer Forums 'Swift' tag as the vendor-run official Q&A channel, (4) the top independently-documented third-party tutorial/book ecosystem for the language (identified via search rather than picked by the benchmark), and (5) StackShare's per-language discussion/follower counts, used only as one proxy among several, never standalone.

component_findings.current_knowledge: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-3--swift): Apple's official developer forums maintain an active, current 'Swift' tag with recent (multi-day-old) technical Q&A threads, indicating an actively used vendor-run public knowledge channel distinct from the community-run forums.
component_findings.events_groups: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-3--swift): Community and ecosystem-project discussion volume on the official forums has grown over time, with a dedicated 'Related Projects' category added to accommodate ecosystem growth, and recurring community events (e.g., Embedded Swift Community Hour).
component_findings.international_breadth: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-3--swift): Swift scores high (85/100) reflecting: (a) a mature, official, well-structured community forum; (b) a second, actively used vendor (Apple) Q&A channel; (c) a historically very large and fast-growing Stack Overflow presence plus a top developer-sentiment survey result; and (d) an unusually deep, independently corroborated third-party tutorial/book/course ecosystem. It is not scored at the very top of the range because its public knowledge base is more platform-concentrated (Apple ecosystem) than the most universally-discussed general-purpose languages, and because some precise current-volume figures (exact live SO tag count) were not obtainable within the retrieval budget, so qualitative/tren
component_findings.learning_materials: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-3--swift): Swift has an unusually large independent third-party learning-content ecosystem: Kodeco offers extensive free content plus books and high-quality tutorials, and Hacking with Swift's author is described as one of the most prolific iOS educators, continuously publishing and updating a library of books; additional community-run resources include the Try Swift conference series and Swift by Sundell.
component_findings.qa_discussion: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-3--swift): The Swift forums are the official discussion channel for the Swift community and the best place to connect with other Swift developers (swift.org/community); forum migrated from mailing lists with dedicated subcategories for Compiler, Standard Library, Core Libraries, Package Manager, LLDB, Server, etc.

metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.limitations: StackShare stack/follower counts are a raw popularity proxy and are not used standalone; they corroborate but do not independently establish the score. | Swift's public knowledge base is more concentrated around Apple-platform (iOS/macOS) use cases than general-purpose programming discourse, so breadth outside that domain (e.g., server-side/embedded Swift) is comparatively thinner, though growing (per Embedded Swift Community Hour activity). | Raw counts (StackShare followers, historical SO tag growth) are proxies with known limitations per methodology and are corroborating evidence only, not the sole basis for the score.
metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.selection_rule: Inspect the same knowledge channels for every language and use current, publicly accessible evidence rather than raw search-result counts alone.

snapshot_recertification.policy: legacy evidence re-adjudicated under current runner-owned rubric
